records.finding: The fire occurred during the Apollo 204 plugs-out ground test.
records.limit: This test context alone cannot establish the exact ignition source.
records.source: Report of the Apollo 204 Review Board
records.title: A ground test, not a launch

records.finding: The Board recorded a 100-percent oxygen test atmosphere at approximately 16.7 psia and judged the conditions extremely hazardous.
records.limit: This finding describes the hazard; it does not by itself identify a specific ignition location.
records.source: Report of the Apollo 204 Review Board
records.title: Oxygen and pressure made the cabin hazardous

records.finding: The Board determined an electrical arc was the most probable initiator.
records.limit: The Board explicitly reported that no single ignition source was conclusively identified.
records.source: Report of the Apollo 204 Review Board
records.title: Most probable does not mean proved

records.finding: The accident inquiry documented hatch-opening and escape constraints during the fire.
records.limit: A summary of hatch constraints is not a substitute for the Board’s full technical sequence.
records.source: Report of the Apollo 204 Review Board
records.title: The escape problem

records.finding: NASA’s retrospective describes 102 deliberately initiated Command Module fires in tests conducted from December 1967 through February 1968.
records.limit: These later engineering tests did not identify the original Apollo 1 spark. The article was published in 2018, not during the accident investigation.
records.title: The later flammability program
